title: Plan of the summary by books and volumes
english: Epiphanius writes: And returning again, I will divide them by book and show in this summary how many of these eighty heresies are in the first book, then in order in the second, and through to the third. I will also show, for each of the seven volumes arranged within the three books, how many heresies each one contains. It is as follows: the first book has three volumes and forty-six heresies, with their names, namely Barbarism, Scythianism, Hellenism, Judaism, and Samaritanism. [list continues] The second book has two volumes and twenty-three heresies. The third book has two volumes and eleven heresies. To return to the first book: the first volume contains twenty heresies, which are these: Barbarism, Scythianism, Hellenism, Judaism.

added_allusions.reason: Apostolic neither barbarian nor Scythian frame of early ages (cross-ref Panarion Cap. I)

orientation: Epiphanius is opening his summary by explaining how he will lay out the count of the eighty heresies across the books and volumes of his work.
